newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada sees new salmon talks with U.S.
newsitem.headline: Canada sees new salmon talks with U.S.

text.p: Canada and the United States will likely head back to the bargaining table to resume talks on Pacific salmon fishing that collapsed last month, Canada's Foreign Affairs Minister Lloyd Axworthy said on Thursday.
"We feel we could get back to the table next week, but I'll know more exactly by the end of this week," Axworthy told reporters after a cabinet meeting.
Canada and the United States have skirmished for years over salmon catches in the Pacific Northwest and pressure for a deal is mounting before this year's salmon run, which begins in a few weeks.

In May, the Canadians walked out on talks when U.S. negotiators said they were not authorized to offer a specific catch reduction at the session. Canada is concerned about overfishing by American boats as salmon head through Alaskan waters into Canadian waters to breed.

Canada seized four U.S. boats after talks broke down last month, enforcing existing regulations against U.S. boats as a sign of its frustrations. The boats were released after paying small fines, but the United States said the actions poisoned the atmosphere for discussions.
But Axworthy said on Thursday he had spoken with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright a day earlier and was encouraged.
"I think there's an interest to restart negotiations, but we have to have another exchange," Axworthy said.
"In the last discussions, there was a fair degree of closure on a lot of the items."
